subject: Post-call: Exec recap & procurement path - AuroraMed
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Miriam Santos <miriam.santos@auroramed.com>, Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@auroramed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Exec recap & procurement path - AuroraMed

Hi Miriam / Kyle —

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the candid conversation. Quick exec-level recap and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of need / business outcomes:
- Current challenge: high latency and burst costs on clinical note generation pipeline; peak windows causing delayed availability for providers.
- Goal: reduce per-token cost by 40% and achieve P95 latency <350ms for the clinician-facing flow to meet SLAs.
- Desired outcome: faster charting, fewer provider timeouts, measurable reduction in operational GPU spend.

Key risks called out on the call:
- Security/compliance (SOC 2 + data residency) and procurement approval timeline.
- Integration effort for prefix caching into your legacy transformer wrapper.

Procurement path / timeline (as discussed):
- Budget window: Q2 approval preferred (you mentioned target by end of April).
- Procurement owners: Kyle (procurement) + CISO (security sign-off) — need to loop both into the MA P.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) Sean: share one-page exec recap + draft SOW (attached) — ACTIONED (see attachments).
2) Miriam / Kyle: confirm procurement window and list any required security artifacts (SOC2, pen test reports).
3) Schedule technical architecture review with your infra/CISO team (30–45m) — propose next Tue/Wed.
4) Redwood: prepare mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and delivery SLAs; include fallback options (quantized model variant) if cost/latency trade-offs required.

Please reply with any corrections, confirm procurement timeline, and availability for the architecture call. If helpful I can prep a one-pager for your CFO that summarizes expected cost savings and ROI.

Attachments: AuroraMed_MATP_Exec_Recap_20270217.pdf, SOW-draft-v1.docx

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Dr. Miriam Santos <miriam.santos@auroramed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@auroramed.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Exec recap & procurement path - AuroraMed

Thanks Sean — good write-up and appreciate the clear next steps. A few quick notes from our side:

- Procurement window: Q2 looks right; finance is targeting vendor approvals by end of April but it depends on security sign-off.
- Security: our CISO has asked for SOC 2 Type II, a recent pen-test summary, and an architecture diagram showing how PHI is isolated and encrypted at rest/in transit. Can you provide those?
- Scope: the pilot we described would start with the ED charting flow (~10k monthly active users) and then expand to ambulatory if results meet latency/cost targets.

Kyle — looping you since you’ll own the PO and contracting. Kyle, can you confirm whether AuroraMed requires our standard procurement addendum or if we can proceed with Redwood’s standard SOW + DPA?

Appreciate the ROI one-pager — that will help with CFO conversation. For the architecture call, Tues 2/23 or Wed 2/24 afternoon PT works for our infra team.

Thanks Miriam — that timeline and list of artifacts makes sense. Quick replies and proposed MAP: 

1) Security artifacts: Laura (cc'd) will send SOC 2 Type II report + pen test summary and an architecture diagram (redwood-hosted control plane + customer VPC options).
2) Pilot scope confirmed: ED charting flow to start (~10k MAU).
3) Proposed MAP / milestones (we'll produce a formal MAP doc):
   - Week 0: Contract signature + initial onboarding (procurement + legal).
   - Week 1–2: Architecture review & security Q&A with your CISO.
   - Week 3–6: Pilot deployment (dedicated capacity) + weekly check-ins; success metrics = P95 latency <350ms and 40% cost reduction.
   - Week 8: Pilot review and decision on expansion.
4) SOW: attached draft SOW includes timelines and acceptance criteria — please feel free to redline.

Kyle — can you confirm whether AuroraMed will use your procurement addendum or if you prefer Redwood's standard SOW + DPA? If you want the addendum we can have legal prep a redline before the call.

Miriam — we're available Tue 2/23 10:00–11:30 PT or Wed 2/24 13:00–15:00 PT for the architecture call. Let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite with the agenda.

Thanks —
Sean
(sean.gallagher@redwood.ai)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Exec recap & procurement path - AuroraMed (internal)

Heads up — forwarding the thread with exec recap from yesterday. Quick internal summary / asks: 

What we heard:
- AuroraMed wants to run ED charting as a pilot with clear cost/latency SLAs. Procurement wants approvals by end-April.
- Security is the gating factor: CISO needs SOC2 Type II, pen-test summary, and an architecture diagram showing PHI separation.

Risks / escalation items:
- If SOC2 + pen test artifacts aren't provided promptly, procurement timeline slips — impact to Q2 bookings.
- Potential price pushback if pilot performance doesn't show >30% cost savings in first 6 weeks.

Internal asks (owners):
- Laura: please send SOC2 Type II report + pen test summary and a one-page security FAQ by EOD today so I can share with Miriam.
- Marissa: draft a short MAP doc and a CFO-facing ROI one-pager (numbers based on a 40% per-token reduction) by EOD Mon.
- Aditya: be ready to support the architecture call; prep slides on our caching/batching and quantization options.
- Legal: anticipate SOW redlines and procurement addendum requests — if we can, propose 30-day turnaround on redlines.

I'll capture these in the deal record (HubSpot) and set up the architecture call once Miriam confirms a slot.

Thanks — Sean
